question: Which defects in character does the name "Pride and Prejudice" primarily refer to?

options.text: Lydia’s erratic behavior and Wickham’s deceits
Arrogance of Lady Catherine and Mr. Collins’s servility
Mr. Bennet’s wit and Mrs. Bennet’s fussiness

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Literal Interpretation of the Title:***

 
 
• The passage states: "The title itself is quite meaningful, as it first indicates the character flaws that drive much of the conflict in this novel."
 
 
 
• ***Direct Character Association:***
 
 
• The text explicitly links the two terms to the protagonists: "Darcy’s pride and Elizabeth’s prejudice."
 
 
 
• ***Reasoning for the Flaws:***
 
 
• Pride: Darcy is described as showing a "haughty character" and being "superior by virtue of his class."
 
• Prejudice: Elizabeth is noted to have "very quickly showed prejudice against him" after being offended by his lack of warmth and misled by Mr. Wickham.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Darcy’s pride and Elizabeth’s prejudice.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect. While these are character traits mentioned, they do not define the primary meaning of the title's "Pride" and "Prejudice."
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect. These characters symbolize class consciousness and "hard and silly aspects" of the social structure, but are not the primary subjects of the title.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect. These traits provide humor and contrast in the Bennet household but do not represent the central character defects of the title.
